Assume Countable Choice. Let $\Sigma$ be a closed connected Riemann surface, $X=\operatorname{Sym}^m(\Sigma)$ with its standard complex structure, and $m\ge1$. For $a\in\Sigma$ put $E_a=\{a\}+\operatorname{Sym}^{m-1}(\Sigma)$. This is a smooth complex hypersurface, including at repeated tuples. The universal incidence hypersurface $\mathcal E=\{(a,D):D\in E_a\}\subset\Sigma\times X$ carries a smooth complex divisor line bundle with its canonical section, whose zero set is $\mathcal E$ with multiplicity one.

For a smooth map $v:S\to X$, where $S$ is an oriented sphere or a closed disk, define $n_a(v)$ as the degree of the pullback point-divisor line bundle; for a disk use the canonical section to trivialize it on the boundary, and require $v(\partial S)\cap E_a=\varnothing$. The proof constructs this integer by elementary frame winding. It is defined even when a sphere lies wholly in $E_a$.

For a sphere, $n_a(v)$ is independent of $a$ on all of $\Sigma$. For a disk whose boundary tuples have all entries in a finite union of curves $\Gamma\subset\Sigma$, it is independent of $a$ on each connected component of $\Sigma\setminus\Gamma$. If $v^{-1}(E_a)$ is finite and the map is holomorphic on a neighborhood of every one of these points, then
$$n_a(v)=\sum_{z\in v^{-1}(E_a)}\operatorname{ord}_z(F_a\circ v)\ge0,$$
where $F_a$ is any local holomorphic defining function of the smooth hypersurface $E_a$. Each term is a positive integer. Thus the degree agrees with proper holomorphic intersection multiplicity, while divisor containment is handled by its degree definition and actual point movement rather than an unsupported proper-intersection assumption.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $\Sigma$ be a closed oriented genus-$h$ Riemann surface with a supplied orientation-compatible finite polygon presentation as in the finite diagonal-degree theorem, and let $m\ge1$. Put $X=\operatorname{Sym}^m(\Sigma)$. For every smooth sphere map $u:S^2\to X$ and every $z\in\Sigma$, define $n_z(u)$ to be the degree of $u^*\mathcal O(E_z)$, where $E_z=\{z\}+\operatorname{Sym}^{m-1}(\Sigma)$ and degree is finite face winding, including when the sphere image is contained in $E_z$. Then
$$\deg(u^*\det_{\mathbb C}TX)=(m+1-h)n_z(u).$$
In particular this formula is valid for arbitrary smooth sphere classes, not only holomorphic maps or simple incidence curves. It is unchanged on replacing the standard complex tangent bundle by a homotopic complex structure on the same real tangent bundle.

Let a smooth fixed-end Whitney strip model with actual product end frames represent a class $\phi$, and let $\phi\#u$ be its interior connected sum with such a sphere, using a specified attaching path and keeping the physical boundary and end data fixed. Its actual real Fredholm indices, before source translation, satisfy
$$\mu(\phi\#u)-\mu(\phi)=2(m+1-h)n_z(u).$$
Thus when $m=h+k-1$ the sphere shift is exactly $2k\,n_z(u)$. This includes all positive and negative sphere degrees. In particular the finite polygon can be constructed, rather than separately supplied, when $\Sigma$ bounds a smooth handlebody embedded in $S^3$ with $m=h+k-1$ smooth proper rank-two compression disks cutting it topologically into $k$ balls. This application permits tangential disk boundaries: auxiliary disk replacement and smooth cut-ball reconstruction are proved prerequisites below. No full domain/corner formula for a nonspherical Whitney class, boundary-degeneration count, absolute grading or invariance theorem is included.

Assume countable choice. Let $X$ be a compact smooth manifold with a smooth path $J_t$ of almost complex structures, and let $L_0,L_1$ be compact submanifolds totally real for $J_0,J_1$, respectively. Suppose their intersection is finite and transverse. At each intersection point choose a target chart in which $L_0=\mathbb R^m$, $L_1=i\mathbb R^m$ and $J_t=i$ for every $t$. Retain those same charts and structures throughout.

A smooth fixed-end representative from $x$ to $y$ is a smooth map $u:\mathbb R\times[0,1]\to X$ with boundary on $L_0,L_1$, identically $x$ on one full negative tail and identically $y$ on one full positive tail. Its covariant Cauchy–Riemann linearization on fixed-end $H^1\to L^2$ spaces is Fredholm. Its real index is independent of the chosen smooth connection and of the representative under any smooth relative homotopy $H(h,s,t)$ with those boundary conditions, fixed endpoints, and one common pair of constant tails for all $h\in[0,1]$.

These indices add under concatenating two such representatives at their common endpoint, are zero for a constant representative, and change sign when $u(s,t)$ is replaced by $u(-s,t)$. Thus they define an integer index on smooth fixed-end representatives modulo the stated smooth relative homotopies, with concatenation and reversal laws. This result includes nonholomorphic representatives. It does not assume that a nonlinear moduli space exists or is regular.

A further relative smoothing and end-flattening argument is required to identify this smooth quotient with a Whitney-class set defined initially by arbitrary continuous disk maps and continuous relative homotopies. No such identification, domain Euler formula, or arbitrary-class representativity theorem is asserted here.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $E\to\overline{\mathbb D}$ be a smooth complex vector bundle of rank $m\ge1$, with complex multiplication $J$, and let $F\subset E|_{\partial\mathbb D}$ be a smooth oriented totally real real subbundle of rank $m$. Let $P$ be a smooth real-linear first-order operator on sections with exact Cauchy–Riemann symbol: for real smooth $h$ and smooth $\xi$,
$$P(h\xi)=hP\xi+h_x\xi+h_yJ\xi.$$
Use smooth positive definite metrics and finite smooth charts to define $H^r(E)$ by weak derivatives for integers $r\ge1$. Let $X_0$ be the $H^1$ closure of smooth sections with boundary values in $F$, and put $X_q=H^{q+1}(E)\cap X_0$, $Y_q=H^q(E)$ for integers $q\ge0$. Only the zeroth boundary condition is imposed.

There is a smooth global complex frame of $E$ and an integer $k$ in which the boundary condition is
$$F(e^{it})=e^{ikt}\mathbb R\oplus\mathbb R^{m-1}$$
and the actual operator is $\partial_x+i\partial_y+B$ with smooth real-linear zeroth-order coefficient $B$. Equivalently, before this reduction, if $C(t)$ is the complex matrix whose columns are any smooth periodic oriented real frame of $F$ in any global complex frame, then
$$k=\frac1{2\pi i}\int_0^{2\pi}\frac{(\det C)'(t)}{\det C(t)}\,dt.$$
Such frames exist, and this integer is independent of both choices.

Every actual realization $P_q:X_q\to Y_q$ is bounded Fredholm with real index $m+2k$. Its kernel is the same set as the $H^1$ kernel, its range is $Y_q\cap\operatorname{Ran}P_0$, and inclusion in $L^2$ identifies its real cokernel with that of $P_0$. For $\xi\in X_0$ and $P\xi=f\in H^q$,
$$\|\xi\|_{H^{q+1}}\le C_q(\|f\|_{H^q}+\|\xi\|_{H^1}).$$
The inverse of $P_0$ from its $H^1$ kernel complement to its closed range is bounded, and its restriction gives a bounded range inverse $H^q\cap\operatorname{Ran}P_0\to X_q$. The statement applies to an actual geometric linearization along a smooth disk with oriented totally real boundary. It does not assert its surjectivity, compute a Heegaard domain formula, or supply a puncture or gluing theorem.

For a proper smooth map $F:M^n	o N^n$ between nonempty connected oriented smooth boundaryless manifolds, the scalar in the degree definition exists uniquely. Every $
u\in\Omega_c^n(N)$ with $\int_N
u=1$ satisfies $\deg(F)=\int_MF^*
u$. This value is independent of the normalized form, and for every compactly supported top form $\omega$ it satisfies $\int_MF^*\omega=\deg(F)\int_N\omega$. All assertions are choice-free.

Let $F:M^n\to N^n$ be a proper smooth map between nonempty connected oriented smooth manifolds without boundary. If $y\in N$ is a regular value, then its fibre is finite and
$$\deg(F)=\sum_{p\in F^{-1}(y)}\operatorname{sgn}(dF_p)\in\mathbb Z.$$
An empty fibre gives the empty sum zero. In dimension zero the signs compare the supplied determinant-line rays. The formula is choice-free and presupposes only a given regular value, not a theorem asserting their existence.

Let $M^n$ be an oriented smooth manifold without boundary. For each compact set $K\subseteq M$ there are finitely many nonnegative smooth functions $\chi_i$ with compact supports contained in connected coordinate domains $U_i$, such that $\sum_i\chi_i=1$ on a neighbourhood of $K$. For $\omega\in\Omega_c^n(M)$ define
$$\mathcal I_M(\omega)=\sum_i I_{\phi_i}(\chi_i\omega)\quad(K=\operatorname{supp}\omega),$$
using the signed chart integrals. This value is independent of the finite functions and charts. It defines a linear functional, is local under restriction to an open set containing the support, and for $n\ge1$ satisfies
$$\mathcal I_M(d\eta)=0\qquad(\eta\in\Omega_c^{n-1}(M)).$$
For $n=0$ it is the finite signed sum $\sum_{p\in\operatorname{supp}\omega}\varepsilon(p)\omega(p)$. All assertions are choice-free: no partition on the entire manifold is required.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $\mathcal F:M\times S\to N$ be a smooth family of maps and let $Z\subseteq N$
be an embedded submanifold. If $\mathcal F\pitchfork Z$, then the set of
parameters $s\in S$ for which the slice $\mathcal F_s:M\to N$ fails to be
transverse to $Z$ is a null subset of $S$.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $F:M\to N$ be a smooth map between smooth manifolds. Then the critical value
set of $F$ is a null subset of $N$.

derivations.claim: Replace either model by a smoothly homotopic one, fixing its whole boundary collar and corner neighborhoods, which misses all higher multiplicity strata and is transverse to the simple-double-root stratum. Use the finite supported coordinate variations of [F2]'s proof, multiplied by a source cutoff. They span the target tangent at every point in a compact neighborhood of the original repeated-point preimage; the frozen boundary collar misses that locus because the product tori have distinct roots and the disk map is continuous. Choose the variation sufficiently small that no new repeated tuple occurs outside that neighborhood, using positive separation on its compact complement. Thus [F5] applies there and transversality is vacuous on the frozen collar. The new repeated-point preimage is finite. The same ordered-cover construction as [F2] gives a degree-$d=m!$ compact oriented smooth branched cover $\pi:F\to\overline{\mathbb D}$ and ordered smooth roots $f_l:F\to\Sigma$. At a positive double collision use a root coordinate $\zeta$ and at a negative one $\overline\zeta$; in each case $\pi$ preserves orientation. This is a smooth map construction, not an assertion that the perturbed model is holomorphic. Relative point-divisor degrees and actual index remain unchanged by [F1]–[F3]. [F1, F2, F3, F5, given, construct]

For every region $R$, the coordinate degree sum is $$\sum_l\deg(f_l;R)=d\,n_R(u).$$ Indeed every coordinate boundary is on the curve system, so its restriction over $R$ is proper. Choose in $R$ a common regular value for the finitely many roots, missing the finitely many branch-point coordinate values; [F5] supplies it, with empty fibers allowed. The local point-divisor equation is the product of the root coordinates minus that point. At its inverse points the covering is unbranched, so the signed intersection count is the sum of the signed coordinate counts, with exactly $d$ ordered lifts of each original inverse point. [F4] identifies these counts with the coordinate degrees, and [F1] identifies the divisor count with $n_R(u)$. Equivalently use the local product-definer line identity, which gives the same winding equality. This proves the formula for arbitrary smooth models, including negative local intersections. The same construction applies to $v$ with the same $d$. [F1, F4, F5, step 1.1, construct, algebra]

Order the coordinates of a boundary tuple by its attaching-circle labels, possible uniquely because the circles of one family are disjoint. Along an alpha boundary arc the root on $\alpha_i$ is therefore one specified path $a_i^u$; every ordered sheet has exactly one coordinate equal to that path. Thus the total lifted coordinate boundary contains EXACTLY $d$ copies of it. The beta paths $b_j^u$ have the reverse source-boundary orientation, and the same multiplicity statement holds. Constant corner intervals contribute zero. For $u$ and $v$ the differences $a_i^u-a_i^v$ and $b_j^u-b_j^v$ are closed circle loops. Write $w_i,\widetilde w_j\in\mathbb Z$ for their angular windings with the source-boundary signs. Finite argument lifts give these integers; integrating any circle one-form is its mean times this winding, because the zero-mean part has a periodic primitive. Hence for every smooth surface one-form $b$ the difference of the total lifted coordinate boundary integrals is $$d\left(\sum_i w_i\int_{\alpha_i}b+\sum_j\widetilde w_j\int_{\beta_j}b\right).$$ In the one-torus case there is just the corresponding one-family sum. [step 1.1, construct, algebra]

Fix an open edge of an attaching circle away from opposite-family intersections, oriented as the $x$ axis in a positive $(x,y)$ chart. Take $b=\rho(x)\chi(y)\,dx$ supported there with $\int\rho=1$ and $\chi(0)=1$. Its derivative integrates as $+1$ on the positive side and $-1$ on the negative side. Apply compact Stokes to each lifted root surface, then the two-form degree formula [F4] over the regions, and subtract the two models. The inverse images of curve edges add no two-form integral: on the rank-deficient set the pullback vanishes, and on the regular set each preimage is locally a smooth arc of measure zero; a countable coordinate cover suffices under Countable Choice. The two preceding steps give $$d\big((n_+^u-n_+^v)-(n_-^u-n_-^v)\big)=d\,w_i$$ for an alpha edge, or $d\widetilde w_j$ for a beta edge. Both sides of a nonseparating edge may be the same region, in which case its difference is zero. The right side is constant along every open edge of that full attaching circle; hence the coefficient jumps describe exactly its full-circle boundary with the stated winding coefficient. This proves the periodic-domain assertion without assuming equality. If $D(u)=D(v)$, all these integers vanish. Every circle has such a local edge, even a circle with no opposite-family crossing. Thus all labelled boundary-path winding differences are zero. No inference from merely homologically vanishing boundary chains was made. [F4, step 2.1, step 2.2, construct, algebra]

Parametrize each labelled circle by $\mathbb R/2\pi\mathbb Z$ and lift its two paths to real paths with the same initial lift. Their final lifts agree by step3.1. Linear interpolation between those lifts is an explicit homotopy relative both endpoints. Taking the products gives separate alpha and beta boundary homotopies inside their actual product tori, fixing both generators. Reparametrize paths to be constant near the marked endpoints, as the original models already are; this makes the two arc homotopies glue smoothly at the corners. In the one-torus case their based loop lifts have the same initial and final values and the same interpolation gives a based homotopy. Glue $u$, the boundary homotopy cylinder, and the orientation reversal of $v$ to obtain a sphere map $A$. Smooth its collars by constant-end reparametrizations; any remaining finite coordinate seams can be smoothed by straight coordinate interpolation, with values fixed on smaller collars. This does not alter the disk classes or the boundary torus homotopies. For any region point $z$, the cylinder image avoids $E_z$ and its canonical section is nonzero there. Relative degree additivity by face winding therefore gives $n_z(A)=n_z(u)-n_z(v)=0$. [F1, step 1.1, step 3.1, construct, algebra]

By [F2], the determinant line on this sphere has degree zero. Compare disk determinant frames across the cylinder just as in the sphere-attachment calculation of [F2]. The squared phase difference of the two physical boundary problems is twice that sphere determinant degree: the cylinder carries the prescribed real boundary planes continuously, and every seam argument change cancels except the sphere clutch winding. Therefore [F3] gives equal actual strip Fredholm indices, with fixed end caps unchanged. Its higher Sobolev and smooth weighted realizations have the same index by the cited relative-index theorem. For one-torus disks their Maslov windings agree by the same frame calculation; adding the common $m$ gives equal compact-disk indices, and restricting both to the same bounded fixed-node trace subtracts the same $m$. All statements concern actual smooth realized classes and actual domain degrees. Positive marked multiplicities never entered an exclusion argument, and no formal-domain realization, Euler/corner formula or grading normalization was assumed. [F2, F3, step 4.1, construct, algebra] ∎

boundaries.reason: Actual models and m>=1 are given, not empty source maps.

boundaries.evidence: Steps 1.1 and 5.1 allow constant models, zero domain difference and zero sphere degree.
Steps 1.1 and 2.2 include m=1 with degree-one cover.
Step 1.1 handles arbitrary smooth diagonal coincidences by fixed-boundary homotopy; step 3.1 includes nonseparating edges.
Steps 2.2 and 4.1 retain labelled physical boundary paths, endpoints and prescribed end caps.
Step 1.1 uses finite-dimensional CC transversality only; finite labelled lifts and local degree tests replace AC homology-basis suppliers.

Only actual realized classes are compared.
